findings.lens: ch-safari-fidelity — does the Safari FLOOR actually READ as iOS-27 liquid glass, or a degraded approximation?
findings.verdict: The BE plan is ~80% Safari-comprehensive on the SUBSTRATE truths but ~60% on the FIDELITY bar (does Safari READ as iOS-27, or just "not broken"). The plan's three load-bearing Safari bets all CHECK OUT against source + live WebKit facts: (1) WebKit bug 245510 is confirmed NEW/OPEN as of the latest comment 2026-06-12 — it persists through Safari 26.x, so the WAVE-LIST's "feDisplacement is Chromium-only enhancement INSIDE @supports, floor OUTSIDE" decision (BE.W-LENS-SAFARI) is CORRECT and the existing glass-refract.css:106 gate is already shaped right. (2) The base glass material is genuinely Safari-safe: the unprefixed-in-source backdrop-filter is a DELIBERATE build-time policy (vite.style-assets.ts publishStyleAssets() injects -webkit- into shipped dist, gate-locked by proof:webkit-backdrop) — the SEED's "MUST be Safari compatible" floor is real on the resting plate. (3) The .glass-reveal overlay floor is the data-state form (NOT @starting-style), which is the Safari-robust choice; scroll-driven sits behind @supports(animation-timeline) (Safari 26.0 ships it); useViewTransition feature-detects with an instant fallback. So the floor is NOT broken. BUT the plan UNDER-SELLS three fidelity gaps that decide whether Safari reads iOS-27 vs flat: the lens floor reads FLAT on Safari (no refraction concentration — the single most iOS-defining glass cue is the one Safari loses), the goo-split FLOOR plates are OPAQUE CREAM GEL not glass (morph-bridge.css uses solid radial-gradient fills, zero backdrop-filter), and the plan never resolves whether the goo filter:url() composites correctly OVER the dock's real backdrop-filter glass plates in WebKit (my lens-b probe — the answer affects DOCK-FISSION's whole read). The plan does not hold at the "MATCH-OR-BETTER" bar on Safari without three named hardens. ~62% comprehensive on the Safari-fidelity axis.
findings.findings:
**(a) THE LENS FLOOR READS FLAT ON SAFARI — the most iOS-defining cue is the one Safari loses, and the plan accepts it too cheaply.** glass-refract.css:106 hard-gates the WHOLE refraction behind `@supports (backdrop-filter: url("#glass-refract"))`; bug 245510 (NEW, last comment 2026-06-12) means Safari NEVER enters that block, so it paints `backdrop-filter: var(--glass-blur-resting)` ALONE (glass-refract.css:109) — a uniform blur with NO rim concentration. The squircle edge-lensing (f(x)=⁴√(1−(1−x)⁴), the thin-interior/steep-rim bend at glass-refract.css:14-17) is the SINGLE most recognizable iOS-27 liquid-glass cue, and it is exactly what Safari drops. BE.W-LENS-SAFARI's proposed floor (WAVE-LIST.md:16 — "directional rim + conic --specular-angle edge-glint + --glass-edge-dispersion fringe + a Safari-native layered backdrop") is a DECORATION stack (box-shadow rim + a conic glint + a 0.75px inset dispersion fringe at glass-fx.css:223), NOT a REFRACTION — it cannot bend the backdrop. The plan does NOT probe the one real Safari-native refraction trick available: an `filter: url(#displace)` (NOT backdrop-filter — the regular filter property DOES support feDisplacementMap in WebKit per the MDN/webkit corpus) applied to a CAPTURED/duplicated backdrop layer behind the plate (the iamvdo "faking backdrop-filter using SVG filter" pattern). That is a genuine Safari refraction path the plan leaves on the table — a MATCH-OR-BETTER miss. As specced, Safari gets a FLAT-tinted-blur plate where Chrome gets refraction: the floor reads "frosted glass," not "liquid glass."

**(b) THE GOO-SPLIT FLOOR IS OPAQUE CREAM GEL, NOT GLASS — and the filter:url()+backdrop-filter WebKit composite is UNVERIFIED.** Two distinct problems the plan conflates into "Safari-safe by construction": (b1) morph-bridge.css (the substrate BE.W-DOCK-FISSION generalizes — df-topology/sf-goo name it) has ZERO backdrop-filter (grep count 0); the bridge plates are SOLID warm-cream `radial-gradient(... var(--glass-bg-floating) ... var(--card) ...)` fills (morph-bridge.css:72-77). So during the fission split, the detaching pieces read as OPAQUE GEL DROPLETS, not transparent glass — the backdrop does NOT show through the goo. That is acceptable for the V↔H teardrop (occluded midpoint) but the iOS-27 dock FISSION reference (f_021/f_038/f_040 per df-context) shows the split pieces staying GLASSY/transmissive throughout. The plan's FLOOR is a fidelity DOWNGRADE on the hallmark gesture itself, on EVERY engine, not just Safari. (b2) The deeper unverified risk: if BE.W-DOCK-FISSION instead puts filter:url() goo on a container whose CHILD plates carry `backdrop-filter` (to keep them glassy), that is the known WebKit SVG-filter-ancestor-clips-backdrop-filter-descendant stacking failure — the webcompat/WebKit corpus confirms "complex SVG filters with child elements using backdrop-filter may have rendering/compositing problems in WebKit" and the morph-bridge already concedes `isolation: isolate` (morph-bridge.css:39) creating a stacking context. sf-goo's SHIP DECISION ("filter:url() works in WebKit") is true for the OPAQUE-gel floor ONLY; it is UNPROVEN for any glass-through-goo upgrade. The plan books the WebGL smin tier (BE.W-DOCK-FISSION-WEBGL-TIER) as the fidelity upgrade but never states the CSS floor cannot be both gooey AND glass in WebKit — that constraint is load-bearing and missing.

**(c) THE PER-TRANSITION DEGRADE TRUTHS ARE ASSERTED, NOT RESOLVED — and one is wrong.** BE.W-SAFARI-LIQUID-AUDIT (proof:safari-liquid, WAVE-LIST.md:38) promises "degrade-gracefully-per-transition" but the plan never states the actual Safari-26 support row per BE transition: @starting-style — SHIPS in Safari 26.0 (confirmed, release notes) — but the codebase only uses it on `.glass-top-layer` (animations.css:332, native top-layer dialog/popover); the 11 reka portaled overlays ride `.glass-reveal` data-state (reveal.css:43), which needs `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` + display/overlay transitions (reveal.css:54-60) — and the Safari 26.0 release notes do NOT confirm `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` (my WebFetch returned "no information"). If allow-discrete is NOT in Safari 26, the overlay enter/exit display-discrete leg silently no-ops on Safari and the bloom is HALF-broken (opacity transitions, but the discrete display/overlay legs snap). That is an unverified load-bearing dependency the plan treats as settled. scroll-driven — Safari 26.0 ships animation-timeline (confirmed), and scroll-choreography.css:228 already double-gates `@supports (animation-timeline: scroll()) and (timeline-scope: --gl-pin)` — GOOD, but timeline-scope's Safari-26 status is unverified (the gate is correct either way; this one degrades honestly). view-transitions — same-document startViewTransition is feature-detected with instant fallback (useViewTransition.ts:82-94) — GOOD, genuinely graceful. The plan's gap: it has no PER-TRANSITION support matrix with the actual Safari-26 ship-row for each, so proof:safari-liquid is specced to assert graceful-degrade without the plan KNOWING which transitions degrade vs no-op.

fixes.fix: Add a clause probing the REAL Safari-native refraction path the plan ignores: `filter: url(#displace)` (the regular filter property — feDisplacementMap IS supported in WebKit, unlike backdrop-filter:url, per MDN/webkit corpus) applied to a duplicated/captured backdrop layer behind the plate (the iamvdo fake-backdrop-filter pattern). Decide explicitly: ship it as the Safari refraction floor, OR record WHY the decoration-stack floor (rim+glint+fringe) is accepted as a deliberate fidelity-below-Chrome on Safari. As specced the floor reads FLAT-frosted on Safari, not refractive — name it.

State the load-bearing CONSTRAINT the plan omits: the CSS-SVG-goo floor CANNOT be both gooey (filter:url() ancestor) AND glass (backdrop-filter descendant plates) in WebKit (the SVG-filter-clips-backdrop-filter stacking failure — webcompat/245510-adjacent). The fission FLOOR is therefore OPAQUE CREAM GEL (morph-bridge.css:72-77, zero backdrop-filter), a fidelity downgrade vs the iOS f_021/f_038 glassy split pieces. Either (a) accept opaque-gel pieces as the floor and record it, or (b) book the glassy-split fidelity onto BE.W-DOCK-FISSION-WEBGL-TIER explicitly with the WebKit-stacking rationale as the WHY-not-CSS. Today the plan implies the CSS floor is full-fidelity Safari-safe; it is not.

Build the actual PER-TRANSITION Safari-26 support matrix BEFORE speccing the gate: @starting-style=Safari26.0 ✓, animation-timeline=Safari26.0 ✓, startViewTransition=feature-detected ✓ — but VERIFY `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` (the .glass-reveal display/overlay enter-exit legs at reveal.css:54-60 depend on it) and timeline-scope ship in Safari 26. allow-discrete is the unverified load-bearing dependency: if absent, the 11 reka overlays' bloom enter/exit half-no-ops on Safari (opacity animates, discrete legs snap). The gate must assert the verified row per transition, not a blanket graceful-degrade.

These three are pure color-mix(in oklab)+backdrop-filter+opacity (the ladder.css:43-121 pattern) — genuinely Safari-safe IF they inherit the build-time -webkit- prefix pass (vite.style-assets.ts publishStyleAssets, proof:webkit-backdrop). Add an explicit clause to each: the new backdrop-filter declarations (the iconchip frosted disc, the sheet translucent plate) MUST be enrolled in the proof:webkit-backdrop count-parity so the prefix reaches dist for Safari≤17 — a net-new backdrop-filter surface that the dist-prefix pass misses paints NOTHING on old iOS Safari. Cheap, but currently unstated.

The deep tier (deep.css) re-points --glass-blur-floating to the deep blur via the SAME .glass-floating backdrop-filter rule (deep.css:13-38) — so it inherits the ladder's Safari-safety for free. But the Apple saturate(1.8) blur(18-20px) ceiling is the iOS-27 maximal register; on Safari the heavy blur+saturate is real (no url() needed). Confirm the recorded throttle number is measured on real WebKit/Metal (the BE.W-VIZ-PARITY-METAL roster), not SwiftShader — heavy backdrop-filter blur has a different perf profile on Apple GPUs. Minor, but the 'behind a recorded throttle number' must name WHICH engine.
